context.analysis:
## Overview
An AWS-hosted global online bookstore handling 1 million monthly active users with multi-currency support and secure e-commerce operations. It provides catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized book recommendations.

## Key Elements
- **Customers / Shoppers**: End-users browsing catalogues and purchasing books.
- **Registered Users / Reviewers**: Authenticated customers writing reviews and ratings.
- **Store Administrators**: Internal staff managing content and catalogue accuracy.
- **Online Bookstore System**: Core React/Node.js/Java microservices platform on AWS.
- **Payment Gateway**: Stripe/PayPal handling secure tokenized transactions.
- **Third-Party Shipping APIs**: FedEx/UPS/DHL providing real-time rates.
- **Identity Provider**: AWS Cognito managing OAuth2/OIDC authentication.
- **Analytics & Monitoring Platform**: Datadog/Segment tracking checkout friction and telemetry.

## Relationships
- **Customer to Online Bookstore**: HTTPS (TLS 1.3) via global CDN/WAF and Route 53 latency-based routing.
- **Online Bookstore to Payment Gateway**: HTTPS/REST using tokenized iframe SDKs for PCI-DSS compliance.
- **Online Bookstore to Shipping Providers**: HTTPS/REST with circuit breakers and fallback caching.
- **Online Bookstore to Identity Provider**: OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs.
- **Online Bookstore to AWS Cognito / AWS CloudWatch**: Internal mTLS and AES-256 encryption-at-rest.

## Technology Stack
- **Cloud Infrastructure**: AWS across `us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, and `ap-southeast-1` regions for global resilience.
- **Frontend/Backend**: React SPA with Node.js and Java microservices.
- **Security & Compliance**: AWS WAF, TLS 1.3, AWS Cognito, and AES-256 KMS encryption for GDPR/CCPA and OWASP mitigation.
- **Observability**: AWS CloudWatch, OpenSearch, and synthetic monitoring for 99.95% uptime.

## Rationale
This architecture ensures high availability (99.95%) and low latency (<2s) for 1M MAU through multi-region AWS deployment and edge traffic routing. Security measures like tokenized payments and WAF protection satisfy stringent GDPR, CCPA, and PCI-DSS compliance constraints.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[An AWS-hosted global online bookstore handling 1 million monthly active users with multi-currency support and secure e-commerce operations, providing catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized book recommendations.]
[The system employs isolated microservices deployed across multiple regions to ensure high availability, scalability, and strict compliance with security standards.]

## Key Elements
- Customers / Shoppers [person, context]
- Registered Users / Reviewers [person, context]
- Store Administrators [person, context]
- Online Bookstore System [softwareSystem, context]
- Payment Gateway [externalSystem, context]
- Third-Party Shipping APIs [externalSystem, context]
- Identity Provider [externalSystem, context]
- Analytics & Monitoring Platform [externalSystem, context]
- Single-Page Application (SPA) [container, React, TypeScript, Vite]
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) [container, AWS API Gateway / NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate]
- Catalog & Search Service [container, Node.js / Java, AWS OpenSearch]
- Order & Checkout Service [container, Spring Boot / Go]
- Recommendation & Review Service [container, Python / FastAPI, AWS DynamoDB / ElastiCache]

## Relationships
- Customers / Shoppers -> Online Bookstore System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) via global CDN/WAF and Route 53
- Registered Users / Reviewers -> Online Bookstore System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Store Administrators -> Online Bookstore System via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Online Bookstore System -> Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST using tokenized iframe SDKs
- Online Bookstore System -> Third-Party Shipping APIs via HTTPS/REST with circuit breakers and fallback caching
- Online Bookstore System -> Identity Provider via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs
- Online Bookstore System -> Analytics & Monitoring Platform via HTTPS
- SPA -> API Gateway / BFF via HTTPS/REST and GraphQL
- API Gateway / BFF -> Backend Services via internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript, Vite: Delivers sub-2s page loads on 3G for the SPA hosted globally on AWS CloudFront/S3.
- AWS API Gateway / NestJS on ECS Fargate: Handles request routing, rate limiting, and TLS termination.
- Node.js / Java with AWS OpenSearch: Isolates keyword searches for scalable catalogue browsing.
- Spring Boot / Go with Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL: Ensures ACID-compliant transactions for carts and orders across multiple regions.
- Python / FastAPI with Amazon DynamoDB: Isolates heavy analytical recommendation and review queries from checkout.
- AWS ECS Fargate & App Mesh: Provides Blue/Green deployments, auto-scaling, and internal mTLS service-to-service communication.

## Rationale
[This microservices architecture isolates high-load recommendation queries from critical transactional paths to protect core browsing and checkout performance for 1 million monthly active users.]
[Regional AWS deployment strategies, multi-AZ databases, and aggressive circuit breaking collectively guarantee 99.95% uptime and sub-2-second page load requirements.]

Single-Page Application (SPA).analysis:
## Overview
- An AWS-hosted global online bookstore handling 1 million monthly active users with multi-currency support and secure e-commerce operations.
- Features catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized book recommendations.

## Key Elements
- Customers / Shoppers, Registered Users / Reviewers, Store Administrators
- Single-Page Application (SPA) (React, TypeScript, Vite)
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) (AWS API Gateway / NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate)
- Catalog & Search Service (Node.js / Java, AWS OpenSearch)
- Order & Checkout Service (Spring Boot / Go)
- Recommendation & Review Service (Python / FastAPI, AWS DynamoDB / ElastiCache)
- External Systems: Payment Gateway, Third-Party Shipping APIs, Identity Provider, Analytics & Monitoring Platform

## Relationships
- Customers / Shoppers -> Single-Page Application (SPA): HTTPS (TLS 1.3) via global CDN/WAF and Route 53
- Registered Users / Reviewers -> Single-Page Application (SPA): HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Store Administrators -> Single-Page Application (SPA): HTTPS (TLS 1.3)
- Single-Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF): HTTPS/REST and GraphQL
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Catalog & Search Service: internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Order & Checkout Service: internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Recommendation & Review Service: internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- Order & Checkout Service -> Payment Gateway: HTTPS/REST using tokenized iframe SDKs
- Order & Checkout Service -> Third-Party Shipping APIs: HTTPS/REST with circuit breakers and fallback caching

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript, Vite: Delivers sub-2s page loads on 3G for the SPA hosted globally on AWS CloudFront/S3.
- AWS API Gateway / NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate: Handles request routing, rate limiting, and TLS termination for the BFF.
- Node.js / Java & AWS OpenSearch: Isolates keyword searches for scalable catalogue browsing.
- Spring Boot / Go: Ensures ACID-compliant transactions for carts and orders across multiple regions.
- Python / FastAPI & AWS DynamoDB / ElastiCache: Isolates heavy analytical recommendation and review queries from checkout.

## Rationale
- Microservices architecture on AWS ensures 99.95% uptime and horizontal scalability for 1M MAU across three global regions (`us-east-1`, `eu-west-1`, `ap-southeast-1`).
- Strict decoupling of search, checkout, and recommendation services guarantees sub-2s performance on 3G networks and meets rigorous GDPR, CCPA, and OWASP security standards.

API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF).analysis:
## Overview
[The Online Bookstore System is a scalable AWS-hosted e-commerce platform that provides global customers with catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations.]

## Key Elements
• API Router & Rate Limiter Component (AWS API Gateway)
• GraphQL / REST Resolver Component (NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate)
• Session & Auth Middleware Component (NestJS)
• Telemetry & Logging Interceptor Component (NestJS)
• Regional Distributed Caching (AWS ElastiCache / Redis)

## Relationships
• Single-Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) via HTTPS/REST and GraphQL
• API Router & Rate Limiter Component -> Session & Auth Middleware Component via Internal HTTP
• Session & Auth Middleware Component -> GraphQL / REST Resolver Component via In-process calls
• GraphQL / REST Resolver Component -> Catalog, Order, Recommendation Services via gRPC over mTLS
• API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Identity Provider via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs
• API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Analytics & Monitoring Platform via HTTPS

## Technology Stack
• AWS API Gateway: Provides edge routing, WAF evaluation, and token bucket rate limiting for security.
• NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate: Powers the backend-for-frontend containers with horizontal autoscaling.
• AWS ElastiCache (Redis): Implements regional distributed caching for currency rates and catalogue metadata to reduce latency.
• OpenTelemetry: Standardizes distributed tracing across BFF and backend gRPC services.

## Rationale
[This architecture decouples heavy backend operations from the client while aggregating payloads to achieve sub-2s page loads on 3G networks. Multi-region ECS Fargate deployment and robust edge caching ensure 99.95% availability for 1 million monthly active users.]

Catalog & Search Service.analysis:
## Overview
- Global online bookstore system handling 1 million monthly active users with multi-currency support and secure e-commerce operations.
- Provides catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized book recommendations.

## Key Elements
- Customers / Shoppers
- Registered Users / Reviewers
- Store Administrators
- Payment Gateway
- Third-Party Shipping APIs
- Identity Provider
- Analytics & Monitoring Platform
- Single-Page Application (SPA)
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)
- Catalog & Search Service
- Order & Checkout Service
- Recommendation & Review Service

## Relationships
- Customers / Shoppers -> Single-Page Application (SPA) via HTTPS (TLS 1.3) through global CDN/WAF and Route 53
- Single-Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) via HTTPS/REST and GraphQL
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Catalog & Search Service via internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Order & Checkout Service via internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Recommendation & Review Service via internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS
- Online Bookstore System -> Payment Gateway via HTTPS/REST using tokenized iframe SDKs
- Online Bookstore System -> Third-Party Shipping APIs via HTTPS/REST with circuit breakers and fallback caching
- Online Bookstore System -> Identity Provider via OAuth2/OIDC with short-lived JWTs

## Technology Stack
- React, TypeScript, Vite for global SPA delivery on AWS CloudFront/S3
- AWS API Gateway / NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate for BFF request routing and rate limiting
- Node.js / Java with AWS OpenSearch for isolated, scalable catalogue search
- Spring Boot / Go for ACID-compliant Order & Checkout transactions
- Python / FastAPI with AWS DynamoDB / ElastiCache for recommendations and reviews
- Amazon MSK (Kafka) for asynchronous change-data-capture ingestion

## Rationale
- Microservices architecture on AWS ECS Fargate isolates search, checkout, and recommendation domains to independently scale for 1M MAU.
- Multi-region deployment across us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1 guarantees 99.95% uptime and sub-2s page loads.

Order & Checkout Service.analysis:
## Overview
The Order & Checkout Service provides ACID-compliant transaction processing for carts, secure checkout, and fulfillment within the global AWS-hosted Online Bookstore. It handles multi-currency transactions, ensures strict regional data isolation, and maintains compliance with GDPR and CCPA regulations.

## Key Elements
- Cart Management Component: Manages ephemeral and persistent user cart states.
- Checkout Orchestrator Component: Enforces ACID transactions and coordinates payment/shipping.
- Order Fulfillment Component: Handles asynchronous downstream event dispatch.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-Region: Provides durable relational storage for orders.
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Caches transient cart sessions and multi-currency rates.
- AWS SQS/SNS: Delivers asynchronous event messaging and dead-letter queues.

## Relationships
- API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Checkout Orchestrator Component: Routes gRPC requests with mTLS over AWS Cloud Map
- Checkout Orchestrator Component -> Payment Gateway: Transacts securely via HTTPS/REST using tokenized iframe SDKs
- Checkout Orchestrator Component -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-Region: Executes transactional reads and writes over JDBC/SQL
- Cart Management Component -> AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Accesses cached cart state via RESP protocol
- Checkout Orchestrator Component -> Order Fulfillment Component: Publishes domain events asynchronously via AWS SQS/SNS

## Technology Stack
- Spring Boot / Go: Selected for high-performance, strongly typed microservice implementation.
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-Region: Ensures robust ACID compliance and active-active regional data replication.
- AWS ElastiCache for Redis: Delivers low-latency in-memory session and cart caching.
- AWS SQS/SNS: Provides reliable asynchronous decoupling and fault-tolerant message delivery.

## Rationale
This architecture uses active-active regional deployment and strict ACID boundaries to guarantee 99.95% uptime and reliable 1M MAU scaling. Tokenized payment integration and granular IAM policies eliminate cardholder data exposure while ensuring multi-currency, secure e-commerce operations.

Recommendation & Review Service.analysis:
## Overview
[An AWS-hosted online bookstore handling 1 million monthly active users, featuring catalogue browsing, secure checkout, reviews, and personalized recommendations.]

## Key Elements
- [Online Bookstore System]
- [Customers / Shoppers]
- [Registered Users / Reviewers]
- [Store Administrators]
- [Payment Gateway]
- [Third-Party Shipping APIs]
- [Identity Provider]
- [Analytics & Monitoring Platform]
- [Single-Page Application (SPA)]
- [API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)]
- [Catalog & Search Service]
- [Order & Checkout Service]
- [Recommendation & Review Service]

## Relationships
- [Customers / Shoppers -> Single-Page Application (SPA) via HTTPS (TLS 1.3)]
- [Single-Page Application (SPA) -> API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) via HTTPS/REST and GraphQL]
- [API Gateway / Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) -> Recommendation & Review Service via internal gRPC over AWS Cloud Map / ECS Service Connect with mTLS]
- [Order & Checkout Service -> AWS SQS (Recommendation Queue) via AWS SDK]
- [Recommendation Engine Component -> AWS ElastiCache (Redis) via TCP / Redis Protocol]
- [Review Management Component -> AWS DynamoDB via HTTPS / AWS SDK]

## Technology Stack
- [Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite on AWS CloudFront/S3 for sub-2s page loads]
- [BFF / Gateway: AWS API Gateway / NestJS on AWS ECS Fargate]
- [Recommendation & Review Service: Python / FastAPI on AWS ECS Fargate]
- [Databases & Caching: AWS DynamoDB and AWS ElastiCache (Redis)]
- [Messaging: AWS SQS with AWS KMS encryption]

## Rationale
- [Isolates heavy analytical recommendation and review queries from checkout to protect core revenue and maintain 99.95% uptime.]
- [Employs asynchronous event processing via AWS SQS and caching to handle 1 million MAU with sub-50ms recommendation response times.]
